conflicts.stale_clause: PostgreSQL retains the request fingerprint and exact original response for the lifetime of the affected Trip or durable record; the same key and payload replay that response, while different content returns conflict.
conflicts.replacement_clause: PostgreSQL retains the request fingerprint and exact original status and response for 30 days; the same key and payload replay that status and response during that period, while different content returns conflict.

conflicts.stale_clause: Idempotency receipts preserve principal, command kind, target, key, canonical request hash, expected revision or control version, resulting status, and frozen response reference. They are committed atomically with the bounded mutation or accepted Run. Exact reuse replays the result; another payload conflicts.
conflicts.replacement_clause: After 30 days, the response is removed and a minimal non-sensitive tombstone remains for the affected durable record's lifetime. Later reuse returns a typed expired-key conflict and never executes again.

conflicts.stale_clause: Active and archived Trips remain until explicit Trip deletion or Planner closure.
conflicts.replacement_clause: Trips are automatically deleted 24 months after the later of travel completion and meaningful Planner activity, with advance warning, unless the Planner explicitly deletes the Trip sooner.

conflicts.stale_clause: Trips remain until explicit deletion or 24 months after the later of travel completion and meaningful Planner activity, with warning before automatic deletion.
conflicts.replacement_clause: Trips are automatically deleted 24 months after the later of travel completion and meaningful Planner activity, with advance warning, unless the Planner explicitly deletes the Trip sooner.

conflicts.stale_clause: - Security Audit Records remain for 24 months unless valid privacy deletion requires earlier removal.
conflicts.replacement_clause: - Minimized Security Audit Records remain for one year, subject to earlier removal of identifiable links when privacy deletion requires it.

conflicts.stale_clause: Allow explicit retrieval of superseded Handbook Snapshots with a prominent historical warning while blocking bytes whenever safety, privacy, ownership, access, Evidence, provider, or policy revalidation fails.
conflicts.replacement_clause: Safety, privacy, ownership, or access revalidation blocks historical byte delivery. Evidence, provider, link, or policy invalidation blocks current delivery and regeneration but does not by itself block otherwise lawful explicit historical delivery.
There is no informal Operator legal-hold feature. Any future preservation duty requires a separately reviewed decision and cannot be inferred from Operator authority.

conflicts.stale_clause: Approvals additionally bind the exact Approval Request and reviewed fingerprint.
conflicts.replacement_clause: Pre-commit planning Approval Requests represent an uncommitted proposed result, never a Plan Revision. They bind the proposed-result Fingerprint, accepted base Plan Revision, exact Evidence, and policy reviewed.

requirements.text: As an Operator, I want to bootstrap the first Operator against one exact External Identity, so that administration begins without a permanent universal administrator.
As an Operator, I want to issue a single-recipient Invitation that expires after seven days, so that pilot eligibility remains bounded and application-owned.
As an invited Planner, I want to authenticate with Google federation or an email one-time code, so that I can access Flash Trips without a new password.
As an invited Planner, I want Invitation acceptance to require my matching verified email and authenticated External Identity, so that possession of an Invitation link is insufficient.
As a Planner, I want my access to be associated with stable issuer-and-subject identity rather than email equality, so that identity linking cannot merge accounts unsafely.
As a Planner, I want secure, revocable browser sessions, so that loss of access or suspected compromise can take effect immediately.
As an Operator, I want to suspend or close Planner Access Status without accessing private Trips, so that administration and Trip ownership remain separate.
As a Planner, I want to create a private single-city Trip Request after authentication, so that planning begins from saved authoritative information.
As a Planner, I want to reopen my Trip after refreshing or returning later, so that planning survives browser and process interruptions.
As a Planner, I want only my own Trips to be discoverable or accessible, so that Sensitive Trip Data cannot leak across Planners.

As a Planner, I want Trip Intake to capture goals, dates, city stays, travel legs, party size, preferences, and constraints in typed fields, so that planning does not depend on an ambiguous prompt blob.

As a Planner, I want the initial single-city interface to use a Trip Structure capable of later representing multiple cities, so that my Trip does not require a data-model migration when multi-city planning is enabled.
As a Planner, I want to include optional accountless Companions, so that the plan can cover the people travelling with me without creating collaborator accounts.

As a Planner, I want to record only travel-relevant Companion age categories and typed accessibility, dietary, and mobility constraints, so that planning can respect their needs without collecting private explanations.
As a Planner, I want to select applicable Advisory Authorities for myself and each Companion, so that authority-specific advice is not inferred from identity, language, or location.
As a Planner, I want to provide both a Target Budget and, when necessary, a Hard Budget Limit, so that the product can distinguish a preference from an inviolable ceiling.
As a Planner, I want unsupported destinations or required provider coverage to be rejected before paid work begins, so that I am not charged for a Trip the active portfolio cannot support.
As a Planner, I want to start a Travel Readiness Run for a saved Trip, so that weather, safety, and health considerations are assessed from applicable sources.
As a Planner, I want reconnectable Run progress over a durable event sequence, so that a dropped browser connection does not lose or duplicate the planning state.
As a Planner, I want every Travel Readiness claim to identify its applicable Evidence and observation time, so that I can judge freshness and provenance.
As a Planner, I want global, regional, and selected Advisory Authority health information kept distinct, so that one source never silently substitutes for another audience.
As a Planner, I want missing optional authority coverage shown as a limitation and missing required coverage to block the Run, so that absence is neither hidden nor overstated.

As a Planner, I want Travel Readiness to avoid personalised immigration, legal, vaccine, medicine, diagnosis, exemption, and treatment advice, so that the product stays within its defined safety boundary.
As a Planner, I want provider and model text treated as untrusted input, so that hostile source content cannot control planning or mutate my Trip.
As a Planner, I want a safe explanation when a Run is Blocked, Failed, Cancelled, or succeeds, so that I know what happened and which recovery actions are available.
As a Planner, I want Run status and explanations to omit internal prompts, secrets, chain-of-thought, and private operational details, so that inspection is useful without increasing exposure.
As a Planner, I want to reconstruct why a historical Run executed, skipped, reused, repaired, or blocked work, so that planning outcomes remain accountable.
As a Planner, I want interruption and retry to preserve accepted inputs and terminal history, so that recovery cannot silently rerun against changed context.

As a Planner, I want a single-city Travel Plan built from eligible Accommodation, Dining, Activities, Ground Transport, Route Measurement, Travel Readiness, Budget, and Itinerary results, so that the recommendation is complete rather than a set of disconnected suggestions.
As a Planner, I want only validated Candidates to participate in selection, so that raw Provider Observations cannot become recommendations automatically.
As a Planner, I want provider identity, freshness, scope, market eligibility, attribution, and Evidence requirements checked before a Candidate is usable, so that unsupported data fails closed.

As a Planner, I want the product to evaluate accommodation and transport anchors before dependent places, routes, itinerary, and final budget, so that circular planning dependencies converge predictably.
As a Planner, I want Plan Assembly bounded to at most three Plan Portfolios and one affected discovery expansion, so that planning cannot search or spend indefinitely.

As a Planner, I want every repair to improve hard constraints, schedule conflicts, budget coverage, target-budget excess, or preference fit in a deterministic order, so that the product cannot oscillate or accept a worse plan.
As a Planner, I want no-valid-portfolio results to explain Feasibility Conflicts and possible Constraint Relaxations, so that I can decide what to change without receiving the closest invalid plan.
As a Planner, I want Hard Budget Limits enforced and Target Budget excess disclosed for explicit Approval, so that the product never treats both budget concepts as interchangeable.
As a Planner, I want unknown, ranged, unavailable, and unpriced costs represented explicitly, so that missing cost data is not silently treated as zero.
As a Planner, I want routes, opening constraints, accessibility, dates, local times, time zones, and currencies validated deterministically, so that fluent model output cannot override feasibility.
As a Planner, I want the previous Plan Revision to remain current while a new Run is incomplete, so that speculative or partial results never replace my valid Travel Plan.
As a Planner, I want a successful Run to commit at most one complete immutable Plan Revision atomically, so that I never see a partially updated plan.
As a Planner, I want only one active mutating Run per Trip, so that concurrent planning or amendment actions cannot race into conflicting revisions.
As a Planner, I want a context change before commit to end the Run as Blocked with `context_changed`, so that stale work cannot commit against a newer revision.
As a Planner, I want a plan-first workspace with docked conversation and visible revision provenance, so that structured Travel Plan state remains authoritative while conversation provides support.
As a Planner, I want grounded Trip questions answered against the visible Plan Revision and current Evidence, so that answers distinguish committed facts from newer observations.
As a Planner, I want ambiguous or multi-intent state-changing Turns to produce one focused Pending Clarification, so that the product never guesses my authority.

As a Planner, I want greetings, help, commands, approvals, cancellation, money, dates, and workflow transitions handled deterministically where possible, so that models are used only for bounded interpretation and synthesis.
As a Planner, I want a natural-language change request converted into an untrusted Amendment Proposal, so that I can review typed changes before they affect my Trip.
As a Planner, I want an Amendment Proposal to show its base revision, affected capabilities, invalidations, and unresolved ambiguity, so that I understand the impact before confirmation.
As a Planner, I want only a bound structured action to confirm a Plan Amendment, so that free-text agreement cannot mutate canonical state.
As a Planner, I want stale Amendment Proposals to expire rather than rebase silently, so that every change is interpreted against the Plan Revision I reviewed.
As a Planner, I want an amendment to recompute only affected work whose Fingerprints no longer match, so that valid unaffected results can be reused safely.
As a Planner, I want undo to create a new Plan Amendment instead of deleting history, so that provenance remains intact.
As a Planner, I want cancellation bound to the exact active Run, so that cancelling work cannot delete my Trip or roll back an existing Plan Revision.

As a Planner, I want required Approval Requests presented in deterministic order and bound to the exact facts, revision, Evidence, policy, and Fingerprint reviewed, so that my decision cannot be applied elsewhere.
As a Planner, I want to approve or reject through an explicit bound action, so that a conversational “yes” or conditional statement cannot create Approval.
As a Planner, I want rejection to cancel the current Run without deleting its inspection history, so that a later attempt starts as a distinct Run.
As a Planner, I want expired, superseded, wrong-principal, wrong-revision, or otherwise stale Approvals rejected, so that old consent cannot authorize changed facts.

As a Planner, I want Handbook compilation to begin only when the current Plan Revision, all required Approvals, Evidence, links, and policies remain eligible, so that the delivered artefact matches what I approved.

As a Planner, I want one immutable Handbook Snapshot rendered into semantically equivalent HTML, Markdown, and public JSON exports, so that I can use the same approved content in readable, portable, and machine-readable forms.

As a Planner, I want Handbook Exports to preserve dates, time zones, exact decimal amounts, currencies, unknowns, warnings, citations, and provider deep links, so that rendering does not reinterpret the Travel Plan.
As a Planner, I want Handbook compilation and rendering to perform no live lookups, so that the output is reproducible from its bound canonical records.
As a Planner, I want authenticated private Handbook retrieval without public bearer links, so that offline delivery does not make my Trip public.
As a Planner, I want a superseded Handbook Snapshot available only through explicit historical retrieval with a prominent warning, so that old plans are not mistaken for the current Travel Plan.
As a Planner, I want delivery blocked when safety, privacy, ownership, or access revalidation fails, so that immutable storage does not imply unconditional disclosure.
As a Planner, I want a Handbook Delivery record for each authorized retrieval without treating retrieval as Approval or proof of opening, so that audit meaning remains precise.
As a Planner, I want provider deep links to remain within the non-booking boundary, so that Flash Trips recommends and redirects without taking payment or managing reservations.

As a Planner, I want a provider role enabled only for the exact active market, dates, mode, currency, and coverage profile, so that the product never claims global support from conditional integrations.
As a Planner, I want an equivalent prequalified fallback used only under declared conditions, so that provider failure cannot silently weaken Evidence, attribution, or validation standards.

As a Planner, I want provider deactivation or expired Evidence to derive Revalidation Required for affected selections, approvals, and handbooks, so that historical facts remain immutable while current eligibility fails closed.
As a Planner, I want paid work admitted only after conservative worst-case cost is reserved, so that retries and parallel work cannot exceed policy ceilings.
As a Planner, I want a supported planning Run capped by the active per-Run, per-Planner, environment, and provider limits, so that service cost remains controlled without weakening correctness.
As a Planner, I want exhausted budgets and quotas to return typed outcomes rather than silently choose a cheaper unapproved model or provider, so that cost controls cannot change product truth.
As an Operator, I want to activate and deactivate Provider Market Profiles and terms manifests, so that live providers remain bounded by reviewed markets, rights, attribution, and freshness policy.
As an Operator, I want to issue Paid Execution Authorization for evaluation, provider probes, judging, comparison, and canaries, so that non-product live calls never inherit Planner authority.

As an Operator, I want emergency controls for new sessions, Invitations, model calls, each provider, new Runs, commits, Handbook delivery, and exports, so that an incident can be contained at the affected boundary.
As an Operator, I want aggregate service health, cost, security, and opaque Run references without private Trip content, so that I can operate the pilot without becoming a Trip reader.
As a Planner, I want to enter, reorder, insert, and remove multiple city stays and inter-city legs, so that the same product can support a complete multi-city Trip.

As a Planner, I want cross-city Budget and Itinerary feasibility to account for local dates, time zones, PLN/EUR/CZK conversion, routes, and connection margins, so that each city does not appear valid in isolation while the whole Trip is impossible.
As a Planner, I want Companion Travel Constraints and selected authorities propagated across every applicable city and leg, so that multi-city planning does not lose participant requirements.
As a Planner, I want air-dependent journeys to return an explicit unsupported outcome while Air Travel is inactive, so that ground-supported planning does not pretend to include flights.

As an invited pilot Planner, I want Berlin, Prague, Vienna, and the Warsaw–Berlin–Prague–Vienna acceptance journey enabled only after every mandatory market profile passes its gates, so that advertised support reflects tested coverage.
As a Planner, I want personal-data export, Trip deletion, and Planner closure/deletion through recent-authenticated idempotent actions, so that I retain meaningful control over my data.

As a Planner, I want Flash Trips to refuse passport data, payment data, exact home addresses, medical records, and other unnecessary high-risk information, so that the product minimizes Sensitive Trip Data.
As a Planner, I want no advertising pixels, behavioural analytics, session replay, or nonessential tracking, so that private Trip planning is not repurposed for marketing surveillance.
As a Planner, I want externally visible text escaped or tightly sanitized and links independently validated, so that source or model content cannot execute in my browser.
As a Planner, I want my downloaded Handbook to remain self-contained and script-free, so that it can be used offline without remote required assets.
As a Release Approver, I want promotion bound to an immutable Evaluation Release Record and the exact tested image digest, so that production receives the artefact whose evidence was reviewed.

As a Release Approver, I want any correctness, safety, privacy, authority, or execution-control critical failure to block promotion regardless of aggregate scores, so that quality averages cannot hide severe defects.
As a Release Approver, I want test and production to use isolated identities, data, secrets, and policies, so that non-production work cannot reach production authority or Trip data.

As an Operator, I want the production cohort expanded from one to three to at most ten active Planners only while security, provider, quality, cost, and operational evidence remains healthy, so that the pilot grows under controlled observation.

Flash Trips is a greenfield product. Wanderlisted may supply adapted domain lessons, deterministic algorithms, scenarios, provider knowledge, and evaluation ideas, but its runtime, graph, schemas, APIs, caches, trajectories, and baselines are not compatibility requirements.

The product is initially English-only, invitation-only, and limited to one authenticated primary Planner with optional accountless Companions. Authentication is mandatory before all Trip Intake. Guest Session, Guest General, and Guest Intake Transfer are deferred together.

Booking, payment, cancellation, reservation management, disruption rebooking, and public Handbook sharing remain outside the product boundary. Provider links redirect the Planner to external providers.

The application is a capability-oriented modular monolith with ports and adapters. One installable Python package contains the backend; a Next.js application provides the BFF and separate Planner and Operator surfaces.
The authoritative travel modules are Trip Request, Trip Structure, Air Travel, Accommodation, Dining, Activities, Ground Transport, Travel Readiness, Budget, Itinerary, and Plan Assembly.

Evidence Ledger, Approval, Route Measurement, Workflow Compiler and execution, Reasoning Runtime, RunInspector, Handbook Compiler, identity, providers, and persistence are supporting boundaries with explicit ports.

A deep TripPlanning application façade exposes typed use-case commands, authoritative queries, and replayable Run observation. Conversation is a transport façade over these operations, not the canonical application interface.

Pydantic models are the authored source of truth for external and executable contracts. FastAPI emits versioned OpenAPI, from which a committed typed TypeScript client is generated. Generated contracts are never hand-edited.

The browser uses secure HTTP-only application cookies with origin validation and session-bound CSRF protection. The Next.js BFF retains scoped identity-provider tokens server-side and calls FastAPI through the exact API audience.

Entra External ID is the intended pilot identity provider with Google federation and email one-time-code sign-in. It is accepted only after a disposable contract spike passes authentication, BFF, API validation, Invitation, linking, suspension, bootstrap, local-development, and telemetry requirements. Auth0 is the fallback behind the same OIDC port.

Flash Trips, not the identity provider, owns Invitations, Planner mapping, linked External Identities, Planner Access Status, Operator authority, Trip ownership, Approvals, sessions, and Handbook access. Email equality never creates or links a Planner.

Operators and Planners use distinct authority surfaces. Operator authority grants no access to Trip content. Security-sensitive administration requires recent authentication and immutable Security Audit Records.

Every mutation uses a principal-, command-, and target-scoped idempotency key. The exact original status and response remain replayable for 30 days. A minimal non-sensitive key tombstone remains for the lifetime of the affected Trip or durable record; after the response expires, reuse returns a typed expired-key conflict and never executes the mutation again. The same key with different content conflicts. Trip mutations also bind the expected Plan Revision or control version and never auto-merge stale state.

Bounded local commands commit synchronously. Commands requiring planning execution atomically validate and create a durable Run, then return accepted Run and observation references. PostgreSQL acts as the initial durable queue.

A Run has the lifecycle `accepted → running ↔ awaiting_approval → succeeded | blocked | failed | cancelled` and exactly one terminal outcome. `context_changed` is a Blocked reason, `planner_rejected` is a Cancelled reason, and `superseded` is reserved for immutable revisions and snapshots.

At most one non-terminal mutating Run exists per Trip. Executors use bounded leases and heartbeats. Recovery creates a new attempt within the same non-terminal Run; retries after a terminal outcome create linked Runs.

LangGraph is private workflow machinery. A deterministic compiler builds a DAG from registered Capability Definitions, the accepted Trip Request, the base Plan Revision, Evidence validity, policy, and exact Fingerprints. Models cannot invent dependencies, transitions, approval gates, or canonical commits.

Capability Definitions and injected executors remain separate. Definitions declare typed inputs and outputs, dependencies, inclusion and invalidation rules, Evidence policy, validators, approval triggers, versions, resource limits, execution policy, retry/fallback policy, and terminal failure semantics.

Executors are deterministic, provider-backed, or reasoning-assisted. They cannot mutate canonical state and return either one complete validated result or a typed Blocked or Failed outcome. Skipped and Reused are compiler decisions, not executor outcomes.

Every registered Capability must pass a shared offline conformance contract covering registration, schema compatibility, Evidence, validation, reuse, invalidation, Approval binding, resources, retry, fallback, cancellation, late results, outcomes, inspection, redaction, and fixture-only replay.

PostgreSQL is the normalized relational source of truth. It stores immutable canonical records, small mutable lifecycle controls, and disposable execution records as distinct classes. Transient proposals and graph checkpoints are never promoted in place or treated as canonical state.

Trips are deleted automatically 24 months after the later of travel completion and meaningful Planner activity, with advance warning, unless the Planner explicitly deletes the Trip sooner. Planner closure and privacy deletion retain their shorter blocking and purge rules.

A Plan Revision is a complete immutable Trip-scoped snapshot with a sequential revision number and base reference. Successful planning locks and revalidates the Trip and Run, inserts at most one revision and its selections, updates the current revision, and seals the Run atomically.

Plan changes use base-revision-bound Amendment Proposals and Planner-confirmed Plan Amendments. The previous revision remains current during execution. Dependency-aware recomputation may reuse only exact Fingerprint-matching results that still pass current Evidence, policy, and completion validation.

Evidence is accepted separately from Run-scoped Provider Observations after source identity, scope, freshness, legal eligibility, policy, and domain validation. Evidence and Plan Revision membership are immutable; later invalidation derives Revalidation Required rather than rewriting history.

Plan Assembly evaluates finite Candidates in deterministic stages: validate pools; choose anchor transport and accommodation; calculate a preliminary budget; choose Dining and Activities; measure routes and choose Ground Transport; compile the Itinerary; then produce the final Budget Assessment.

A Run evaluates at most three complete Plan Portfolios and permits at most one affected provider-search expansion. Every repair uses an unseen portfolio Fingerprint and must improve the fixed objective order. Exhaustion returns Feasibility Conflicts and proposed Constraint Relaxations without committing an invalid portfolio.

Conversation Scopes are explicit and every Turn belongs to a closed taxonomy. Deterministic protocol rules precede bounded model classification. Uncertainty, conflicting mutation intent, or schema failure produces a focused Pending Clarification.

Free text cannot approve, reject, cancel, switch Trips, or mutate canonical state. Bound actions identify the exact resource, revision, Approval Request, Run, and Fingerprint. Only one state-changing decision interaction is presented at a time per Trip.

Reasoning Runtime owns versioned purpose-specific profiles for classification, structured interpretation, grounded synthesis, and bounded reasoning. Each profile pins provider, deployment, model compatibility, parameters, schemas, permitted data, prompt, timeouts, fallback, pricing, and evaluation eligibility.

Deterministic code owns facts, Evidence acceptance, safety status, money, dates, permissions, budgets, workflow transitions, Fingerprints, selection acceptance, and rendering. Models produce untrusted proposals and explanations only from minimized, typed inputs.

External cost policy reserves conservative worst-case billable units and monetary cost atomically before dispatch across attempt, Capability, Run, Planner, environment, and provider scopes. Missing, unlimited, unpriced, or unconvertible allowance defaults to zero.

Production policy initially enforces no more than €1 per Run, €10 per Planner over a rolling 30 days, and €100 production-wide over a rolling 30 days, with a measured target of no more than €0.50 for a complete supported planning Run. Infrastructure cost is tracked separately.

Pilot external-cost ceilings are enforced in EUR. Native provider and model billing amounts remain authoritative, while aggregate operational reporting uses USD through a versioned foreign-exchange snapshot. Admission converts conservatively against the EUR ceiling; USD reporting never changes or weakens enforcement.

CI and ordinary local development have zero live-call authority. Evaluation capture, judging, comparisons, probes, and canaries require an exact, expiring Paid Execution Authorization independent of Planner Approval.

Provider adapters own authentication, transport, pagination, and native schema decoding and emit source-specific Provider Observations. Capabilities own eligibility, Evidence, freshness, policy, normalization into Candidates, and deterministic selection.

Providers activate only through versioned Provider Market Profiles and reviewed terms manifests. One primary provider is attempted initially; at most one explicitly equivalent fallback may expand discovery under declared conditions.

The conditional initial portfolio targets Skyscanner for Air Travel; Booking.com Demand with Skyscanner Hotels fallback for Accommodation; Google Places with conditional Foursquare fallback for Dining and Activities; Google Routes with mode-bounded hosted openrouteservice fallback; commercial Open-Meteo with OpenWeather fallback; ExchangeRate-API with applicable ECB fallback; and Tavily with conditional Brave discovery fallback. Activation remains subject to current partner, rights, retention, deep-link, coverage, and cost evidence.
Search results are never Evidence by themselves. Every externally verifiable claim requires a validated source with applicable scope and observation time.

Travel Readiness keeps global, regional, and Advisory Authority sources separate. Initial production requires ECDC regional health coverage, Polish GIS, and an Operator-reviewed Polish travel-advisory authority; mandatory coverage failure blocks admission or execution.

RunInspector stores append-only typed Inspection Records for every Turn and Run, including causality, compilation, workflow decisions, Evidence, validation, attempts, resources, Approval, progress, Plan Assembly, errors, and exactly one terminal outcome. It never treats logs, telemetry, timestamps, or LangGraph state as the authoritative explanation.

Minimized Security Audit Records are retained for one year, subject to earlier removal of identifiable links when privacy deletion requires it. They remain separate from Inspection Records and Application Insights telemetry.

Inspection failure blocks state-changing progress. Audience projections are selected before retrieval: Planners see safe product explanations for their own Trips; Operators see aggregate health and opaque references; production developers do not receive private Trip traces by default.

Run Reconstruction is read-only and performs no execution. Verification Replay uses only complete lawful Replay Bundles with frozen or mocked dependencies, has no canonical commit or Approval path, and produces its own linked inspection outcome.
A Handbook compiles only from the current eligible Plan Revision with all exact required Approvals, Evidence, deep links, and policies still valid and Revalidation Required false.

The Handbook Compiler creates one schema-versioned format-neutral Handbook Document without live lookups. Deterministic renderers produce semantically equivalent UTF-8 HTML, Markdown, and independently versioned privacy-safe public JSON before a snapshot becomes available atomically.

A Handbook Snapshot Fingerprint binds the Plan Revision, qualifying Approvals, Evidence, policies, schemas, compiler and renderer versions, document, exports, and checksums. Exact retries deduplicate; stored bytes remain authoritative and are never regenerated implicitly by newer code.

Superseded snapshots remain explicitly retrievable by their owning Planner with a historical warning while retention and access remain valid. Safety, privacy, ownership, or access revalidation failure blocks byte delivery while preserving audit metadata.

The hosted profile uses GitHub Actions with OIDC, Bicep, Azure Container Registry, Azure Container Apps, Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server, Azure OpenAI, Key Vault, managed identities, and Azure Monitor/Application Insights.

Test and production are isolated. OCI images are built once and promoted by immutable digest without rebuilding. Initial production runs one FastAPI replica with one active mutating Run per Trip and makes no high-availability claim.

West Europe hosts the application, PostgreSQL, registry, secrets, and telemetry. Azure OpenAI may use another approved EU region only when West Europe lacks an eligible deployment and privacy review accepts the data path.

Redis, Service Bus, Front Door, API Management, dedicated workers, multiple replicas, PostgreSQL high availability/read replicas, and other distributed infrastructure remain deferred until measured evidence establishes a need.

Implementation follows eight ordered, deployable slices with no horizontal Phase 0: (1) Invitation to private Trip Request; (2) inspectable fixture-backed Travel Readiness; (3) fixture-backed single-city Travel Plan; (4) Approval to immutable Handbook; (5) typed conversational amendment; (6) qualified live single-city planning; (7) multi-city and Companion-complete planning; and (8) staged invitation-production release.

The initial production cohort is at most ten active Planners from Poland. Supported destination profiles initially cover Berlin, Prague, and Vienna, with Warsaw–Berlin–Prague–Vienna as the canonical multi-city acceptance journey.

Tests assert externally observable behavior, authoritative records, lifecycle outcomes, Inspection Records, security boundaries, and public contracts rather than private implementation structure, LangGraph topology, ORM details, or internal call order unless ordering is itself a contract.

The primary acceptance seam is the versioned JSON/HTTP application boundary: typed commands, authoritative queries, RFC 9457 problem outcomes, and per-Run SSE through FastAPI against real PostgreSQL. Identity, provider, and model ports use deterministic in-process fakes or frozen fixtures by default.

This seam verifies ownership, idempotency, optimistic concurrency, canonical commits, Run lifecycle, Evidence, Approval, Handbook eligibility, reconnectable observation, persistence interruption, and read-after-write behavior through the same contract used by the BFF.

A small browser-journey suite is required for behavior the application API cannot prove: Invitation acceptance and session flow, Planner versus Operator surface separation, structured Trip Intake, refresh/reopen, plan-first revision context, docked amendment review, bound Approval actions, progress reconnection, Handbook download, accessibility, and script-free rendering.

Every Capability and provider adapter must pass its shared offline contract suite. The suite is parameterized over executable contracts and ports and covers all declared outcomes, Evidence classes, invalidation triggers, retries, fallbacks, limits, cancellation, late results, trace completeness, and attempted live-access rejection.

Focused pure deterministic tests are used only where they materially localize correctness for money and currency arithmetic, dates and time zones, Fingerprint canonicalization, eligibility and freshness policy, bounded Plan Assembly repair, itinerary feasibility, renderer semantic equivalence, resource reservations, and typed state transitions.

Persistence tests always use real PostgreSQL rather than SQLite. They cover relational constraints, immutable records, Trip-scoped references, concurrent Run admission and commit, Approval races, leases, idempotency, migrations, retention, deletion, restore scrubbing, and byte preservation.

Contract generation tests fail when OpenAPI or the TypeScript client drifts from Pydantic contracts. Import-boundary tests fail when capabilities, platform modules, adapters, application code, or composition violate their documented dependency directions.

Run and conversation tests verify complete typed Inspection Records, explicit causality, immutable sequencing, exact terminal sealing, redacted audience views, failure on missing inspection, read-only reconstruction, and fixture-only Verification Replay.

Security tests include OIDC and BFF session boundaries, CSRF, Invitation replay and expiry, identity linking, immediate suspension, recent authentication, cross-Planner denial, Operator isolation, prompt injection, provider-content validation, SSRF, browser injection, secret and personal-data canaries, abuse limits, deletion, recovery, and every emergency control.

Handbook tests verify eligibility and revalidation, exact Approval binding, no live compilation calls, schema coverage, semantic equivalence among formats, stable identifiers, byte-for-byte persistence, checksums, citations, deep links, historical warnings, authorization, privacy minimization, and denied delivery.
Evaluation Layer 1 is deterministic and hermetic. Every applicable check must pass; missing, expired, unknown, or unauthorized fixtures fail closed and never trigger live access.

Reasoning Profiles additionally require pointwise semantic judging, pairwise non-inferiority evidence, and human calibration under the accepted thresholds before release eligibility. A Critical Evaluation Failure blocks release regardless of aggregate scores.

Pull requests run formatting, linting, strict typing, import rules, generated-contract drift, affected deterministic tests, shared security cases, migration checks, and OCI builds without live model, provider, or judge calls.

Main and Azure test add real-PostgreSQL integration, persistence and resume, SSE, Handbook, migration, and digest-identified container smoke tests. Live probes and canaries require Paid Execution Authorization.

Production promotion requires a complete Evaluation Release Record bound to the exact commit, image digest, cases, fixtures, baselines, evaluators, models, prompts, providers, policies, results, uncertainty, cost, authorization, independent security review, and approval decision.

The repository is greenfield and contains no existing application-test seam to reuse. The accepted ADRs and throwaway Planner workspace prototype establish behavior, while suitable Wanderlisted cases may seed new Flash Trips Evaluation Cases only after adaptation to these contracts and new ground truth.
Booking, payment, cancellation, reservation management, disruption rebooking, ticketing, or order ownership.
Public signup, Guest Session, Guest General, Guest Intake Transfer, or unauthenticated personalised planning for the invitation release.
Companion accounts, Companion access to Trips or Handbooks, collaborative editing, or coordination between separate Planner accounts.
